 More Than 50,000 Toothpaste and Mouthwash Products Recalled Due to Hormone ‘Cross-Contamination’
 SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY/Getty Images 
 By 
 Alex Vance 
 Published on Nov. 11, 2026
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 A natural oral care brand is at the center, and with expiration dates stretching into 2028, here are the latest details.
 Nowadays, there’s a toothpaste for just about everything, from sensitivity and whitening to tartar control to gum health. Natural toothpastes have also gained popularity, especially among those trying to avoid some of the synthetic ingredients found in conventional options.
 But even products labeled “natural” can still experience some unforeseen issues—and that’s the case with a recent nationwide recall involving more than 50,000 units of toothpaste and mouthwash.
 The recall details
 Scottsdale, Arizona-based ORL Labs LLC is recalling several of its oral care toothpastes and mouthwashes after U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) testing detected the presence of progesterone, estradiol, or dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) in the products. The full FDA explanation reads as, “Cross-contamination: The firm was notified by the FDA of sampling results which found the presence of progesterone, estradiol, or dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA).”
 On November 6, the FDA classified the recall as Class II , meaning the products “may cause temporary health consequences but the probability of a serious health issue is remote.” The recall initially went into effect on October 12.
 Progesterone, estradiol, and DHEA are naturally occurring hormones in the body but are not typical toothpaste ingredients. Progesterone and estradiol play important roles in reproductive health, while the Mayo Clinic explains DHEA as “a hormone that your body naturally produces in the adrenal gland. DHEA helps produce other hormones, including testosterone and estrogen.”
 The recall notice does not explain how the hormone cross-contamination occurred.
 Which products were recalled?
 The recall affects a total of 51,762 units across six ORL oral care products, which can be identified by the following details:
 ORL Organic Oral Care Bubblegum Kids Natural Toothpaste (4 oz.) – 3,976 units 
 UPC: 850006245505 
 Lot numbers: 241029P4 / 250414P4 / 250520P4 / 260406P4 / 260511P4
 Expiration dates: Any expiration date between 9/26 and 8/28
 ORL Organic Oral Care Cinnamint Toothpaste (4 oz.) – 7,202 units 
 UPC: 850006245512 
 Lot numbers: 241209P3 / 250129P3 / 250508P3 / 25112P3 / 260511P3
 Expiration dates: Any expiration date between 9/26 and 8/28
 ORL Organic Oral Care Fresh Mint Natural Toothpaste (4 oz.) – 19,247 units 
 UPC: 850006245499 
 Lot numbers: 250121P7 / 250505P7 / 250508P7 / 250516P7 / 250707P7 / 251105P7 / 260126P7 / 260309P7 / 260422P7 / 260618P7 / 260804P7
 Expiration dates: Any expiration date between 9/26 and 8/28
 ORL Organic Oral Care Bubblegum Kids Mouthwash (16.9 oz.) – 3,116 units 
 UPC: 850006245475 
 Lot numbers: 241029P9 / 250505P9 / 250520P9 / 260406P9
 Expiration dates: Any expiration date between 9/26 and 8/28
 Organic Oral Care Cinnamint Kids Mouthwash (16.9 oz.) – 6,140 units 
 UPC: 850006245468 
 Lot numbers: 241101P10 / 241212P10
 Expiration dates: Any expiration date between 9/26 and 8/28
 ORL Organic Oral Care Fresh Mint Mouthwash (16.9 oz.) – 12,081 units 
 UPC: 850006245451 
 Lot numbers: 240710P6 / 240711P6 / 240807P6 / 241118P6 / 241121P6 / 250120P6 / 250505P11 / 250516P6 / 251105P6 / 260618P6
 Expiration dates: Any expiration Date between 9/26 and 8/28
 According to the FDA, the recalled oral care products were distributed nationwide, though the agency did not specify which retailers sold them. As of November 11, the company’s website displays a notice stating that it is undergoing maintenance and has temporarily paused all orders.
